normative_sections.rationale: RFC 6066 section 1.2 defines BCP 14 terminology rather than an independently implementable protocol behavior; it remains reviewed context and is not assigned to a requirement.

The deprecated max_fragment_length facility is excluded from configuration, offers, and negotiation in favor of Record Size Limit; a bounded peer ClientHello occurrence is ignored opaquely without parsing its body.

Client certificate URL configuration, negotiation, and fetching are excluded; a bounded peer ClientHello occurrence is ignored opaquely without parsing its body or causing network, allocation, cache, or cryptographic effects.

The legacy trusted_ca_keys facility is excluded from configuration and negotiation; a bounded multi-version peer ClientHello occurrence is ignored opaquely while modern certificate-authority selection retains its separate owner.

Truncated HMAC configuration and negotiation are excluded from every modern profile; a bounded peer ClientHello occurrence is ignored opaquely and cannot alter authentication strength, admission, or resumption state.
The PkiPath MIME registration is used only by the configuration-excluded client-certificate-URL facility and creates no supported parsing, fetching, or media-type behavior.

Client-certificate-URL security considerations belong to a configuration-excluded facility; permitted peer ClientHello input is ignored without inner parsing, network effects, redirects, caching, or certificate validation.
RFC 6176 section 1.1 defines BCP 14 terminology and conventions rather than an independently implementable TLS 1.2 behavior; it remains reviewed context and is not assigned to a requirement.
RFC 7301 section 2 defines BCP 14 terminology and conventions rather than independently implementable ALPN behavior; it remains reviewed context and is not assigned to a requirement.
RFC 9853 section 2 defines BCP 14 terminology and conventions rather than independently implementable DTLS RRC behavior; it remains reviewed context and is not assigned to a requirement.
RFC 9853 section 10.3.1 addresses IANA designated-expert administration rather than Brynja runtime behavior; registry reviewers own this guidance outside the DTLS implementation.

authority_deferrals.rationale: SSLKEYLOGFILE is an operational test-support-only facility whose complete production exclusion and packaging review is owned by the residual v0.3.5 closure.
